dartwork — palette explorer

Pick a palette · drag color-count (subset) · toggle B&W / dark-canvas · 9 chart types as chips — click to show/hide each, or quick-pick 3 / 6 / 9 · hover a swatch for hex · copy as Python. All 8-color, CIELAB-generated, B&W + CVD verified.

The system — our own logic

dartwork's palettes follow two organising ideas: a categorical spine on one axis — spectral width (narrow = harmony → wide = distinctness), plus a few intent families for specific jobs. Pick by the shape and job of your data, not by taste:

  • Ordered (rank / amount)? → Sequential, or Neutral if hue carries no meaning.
  • Ordered around a midpoint (±, change, correlation)? → Diverging.
  • Highlight one series, mute the rest? → Focus (teal or warm accent).
  • A few related series? → Analogous (one-mood arc).
  • Two groups? → Duo (warm vs cool).
  • Everyday 4–8 categories? → Trustworthy Default.
  • Many unrelated categories? → Spectrum (full wheel).
  • A specific tone? → Muted, Earth, or Jewel.

Every palette obeys the same engineering rules, so they are interchangeable and dependable:

  • Always 8 colors — need fewer? take a subset (first-N or every-other), built into the ordering.
  • Even CIELAB L* ladder — 8 distinct lightnesses ⇒ all 8 survive black-&-white / print (and most colour-blindness, since CVD preserves luminance). Diverging is the deliberate exception — its two ends share lightness, so it isn't B&W-separable.
  • CVD-verified — deuteranopia / protanopia / tritanopia simulated (colorspacious), not eyeballed.
  • Teal #12a594 is the house anchor, present across the family.
  • Generated, not hand-picked — colours come from gen_palettes.py in CIELAB, so they're reproducible and tunable.
